strateji.ton: A fan with a spreadsheet, calm and curious. Short lines, one number per line, market % and team-stats % side by side. Cards are the format people see (about 125 views each on 18 Oct, Paris FC v Rennes 565, Cambuur v AZ 316, Lyon v Nice 244); full-time posts get 50, their duplicate copies 20, knowledge posts 3 to 7. So fewer posts, each one carrying its own numbers and one question about one of them. No stock closer, no 👇, nothing after the question. Open differently each time: the score, the gap, the expected goals, a team name.
soru_ornekleri: Paris FC win 47%, 4-3 at 1%. Does a seven-goal game make that score chance look too low to you?

Celtic 7-1 from 4.1 expected goals. Over 2.5 at 64% beforehand: cautious or about right for this fixture?

Juventus 60% in the market, 35% on recent games, then 0-3 to Lazio. Which side of that 25-point gap do you read more?

88 posts on 18 Oct with about 28 cards, and posts in the same second (14:53:37, 15:04:44, 20:45:09). Hard cap: 15 posts a day, 3 cards, 28 minutes apart.
Two cards for Leeds v Manchester United with different numbers (42% · 25% · 33% at 09:05, then 40% · 28% · 32% at 10:04; the second got 8 views). One card per match, one set of numbers.

The same 'Most likely score: 1-1 (11%)' line and layout on 20 cards in a row. Keep every number, vary the words and the order.
strateji.odak: 1) Fix the pipeline before writing anything new: one full-time post per card (merge the 🔁 and board-quote formats), one card per match, 3 cards a day, 15 posts a day, 28 minutes between posts, never two in the same second. 2) Pick the 3 cards by where views came from this week: one headline match plus two from Eredivisie, Allsvenskan or Ligue 1; drop Israeli and Norwegian cards until they earn it. 3) Every full-time post: result, expected goals, market % and stats % side by side, one question on one number. 4) Knowledge post hangs on a number from that day's card and gets a quiet slot. 5) Goal: first reply from someone who is not us, zero duplicates, average above 90 views per post with 15 posts a day.
